note: Switch "quarrels" (Quarrels with terms): a man swears before the assembly what he will do to another and by when, and the quarrel is fought by accusation in the assembly. The custom of public accusation is history (docs/research/quarrels.md); the oath with a deadline, every number and every line here are invention.

aims.name: Strip him of his offices
aims.theirOath: have the assembly take {office} from you

history.quote: Dionysius, the son of Hermocrates, taking the floor, accused the generals of betraying their cause to the Carthaginians
history.use: A quarrel is fought by public accusation in the assembly.

history.quote: Philistus, who later composed his History, a man of great wealth, paid the fine and urged Dionysius to speak out whatever he had had in his mind to say
history.use: A friend who pays the fines: the option to spend silver on an accusation.

history.quote: immediately dismissed some of them from office and chose other generals
history.use: An accusation that carries strips a man of his offices.

history.quote: the mercenaries flocked about Dionysius, and the Syracusans in dismay made no move
history.use: Under a tyranny the assembly is cowed: accusations against the tyrant are harder, his own easier.
